# CSS rule reference

Generated from the actual source by [generate-css-reference.mjs](generate-css-reference.mjs). For architecture, cascade hazards and integration recommendations, read [CSS_GUIDE.md](CSS_GUIDE.md). This is a source inventory, not a claim that every historical selector matches the current live game.

## Coverage and reading conventions

- 15 source files: 14 active files in seven lifecycle-owned style tags, plus inactive `header.claude.css`.
- 1542 total blocks: 1426 style rules, 90 at-rule blocks, 26 keyframe steps; 1687 comma-separated selector branches; 6314 declarations, including 4149 marked `!important` and 613 custom-property writes.
- Every declaration is retained verbatim in its source block; later duplicate selectors/properties are separate entries. Source comments immediately before a block are included as author intent, not independent proof of runtime behavior. Comments inside blocks remain in the exact source excerpt.
- Specificity is `(IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, types/pseudo-elements)`, listed in comma-separated selector order. `:is()`, `:not()` and `:has()` use the most specific argument; `:where()` contributes zero. At-rule conditions add no specificity. Inline styles, importance, origin and source order remain separate cascade dimensions.
- Grouping blocks list their exact condition and link to child entries. Each leaf block is reproduced once. Context chains retain nesting. All links identify the source path and starting line.
- Verification: tokenizer reconstruction equals every source character; every curly block is assigned exactly once; an independent `rrweb-cssom` traversal agrees on every rule count, selector, final declaration value and priority. [css-coverage.json](css-coverage.json) contains file hashes, counts and the full structured index. This is syntactic coverage, not rendered-state verification.

Regenerate: `node handoff/technical/generate-css-reference.mjs`. Check drift: `node handoff/technical/generate-css-reference.mjs --check`.

### base-L26 — font-face

[src/styles/base.css:26](../../src/styles/base.css#L26); ends at line 32.

Registers a bundled font face. Family, style, weight range, loading policy and font URL are explicit below; this does not itself assign that font to an element.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 1) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> IdleWorlds Fantasy Skin — "Ashen Iron" base theme
> 
> Visual goal: dense ARPG utility rather than rounded dashboard cards.
> The palette borrows the material language of forged iron, soot, tarnished
> brass and ember without copying any game's assets. Layout remains owned by
> IdleWorlds/React; this layer standardises geometry, typography and surfaces.
> ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> (line 10) ── Typefaces ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> Self-hosted from the extension bundle. These used to come from a Google
> Fonts @import, which had two problems:
> 
> 1. An @import inside a content-script stylesheet is fetched by the PAGE
> and is therefore subject to idleworlds.com's style-src / font-src CSP,
> not to our host_permissions. A CSP tightening on the game's side would
> silently drop every custom face.
> 2. It resolves asynchronously AFTER the rest of the sheet applies, so the
> failure mode was intermittent and cache-dependent — the single most
> likely reason the theme looked right on some loads and not others.
> 
> font-display: swap keeps text visible during load; the src paths resolve
> against the extension root and are listed in web_accessible_resources.
> Run `npm run vendor` to populate assets/fonts/. (Audit S1.2)


**Effect:** Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`font-family`, `font-style`, `font-weight`, `font-display`). Additional CSS settings: `src` = `url('../assets/fonts/cinzel-variable.woff2') format('woff2')`.

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Cinzel';
  font-style: normal;
  font-weight: 600 700;
  font-display: swap;
  src: url('../assets/fonts/cinzel-variable.woff2') format('woff2');
}
```

### base-L74 — style

[src/styles/base.css:74](../../src/styles/base.css#L74); ends at line 193.

Styles global theme tokens and host theme aliases.

**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 79 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
:root {
  /* Forged surfaces */
  --iw-ink-950: #070806;
  --iw-ink-900: #0B0C0A;
  --iw-ink-850: #10100D;
  --iw-ink-800: #14130F;
  --iw-ink-750: #191711;
  --iw-ink-700: #1E1B15;
  --iw-ink-600: #29251C;

  /* ── Per-zone theme accents ───────────────────────────────────────────
     Defaults here reproduce the stock "Ashen Iron" brass/ember exactly. The
     nine :root[data-iw-zone-theme="…"] blocks further down re-point them per
     environment; HeaderRenderer.applyZoneTheme() writes that attribute on
     <html> from the player's current zone (same trigger as the atlas + corner
     filigree swap). Every downstream rule reads a --iw-th-* token — directly,
     or through the --iw-gold / --iw-ember aliases just below — so no rule has
     to know which zone it is. Keep the alias block pointing at -th- tokens. */
  --iw-th-accent:      #D4AD63;  /* bright ornament, hairline peak, focus ring */
  --iw-th-accent-dim:  #9D8458;  /* muted accent, dim labels */
  --iw-th-edge:        #6B4F28;  /* forged 1px frame border */
  --iw-th-hairline:    #9B7437;  /* gold hairline shoulder */
  --iw-th-hairline-hi: #D09A4B;  /* gold hairline peak */
  --iw-th-bracket:     #C9A24D;  /* header corner brackets */
  --iw-th-bracket-dim: #8A7038;
  --iw-th-brass:       #8A6A2C;  /* brass icon tint */
  --iw-th-rule:        #806337;  /* structural warm rule (== old --iw-line-hot) */
  --iw-th-rule-soft:   #3A2F18;  /* faint header rule */
  --iw-th-plate:       #0B0C0E;  /* darkest header-card plate */
  --iw-th-cta:         #B64619;  /* primary action fill (== old --iw-ember) */
  --iw-th-cta-hi:      #D15A22;  /* primary action hover / edge */
  --iw-th-ground-a:    #171713;  /* framed-panel ground gradient, top */
  --iw-th-ground-b:    #0D0E0C;  /* framed-panel ground gradient, bottom */
  --iw-th-ground-wash: transparent;              /* additive per-zone tint over the ground */
  --iw-th-glow:        rgba(226,164,72,.08);     /* inset top bloom on frames */

  /* Inner frame scale. --iw-th-edge frames a PANEL; every box INSIDE one (the
     feed, the queue, a progress track, a stat plate, a row divider) steps down
     from it. These defaults are the stock values the sheets used to hardcode;
     the derived block after the palettes re-points them off whichever
     --iw-th-edge the zone resolved to. */
  --iw-th-edge-mid:    #4A3820;  /* inner box frame: feed, queue, chat input */
  --iw-th-edge-soft:   #332B20;  /* recessed plate, nav rail, column rule */
  --iw-th-edge-faint:  #29251D;  /* hairline divider, control plate edge */

  /* Brass / iron edges */
  --iw-line:    #342D20;
  --iw-line-hi: #58482B;
  --iw-line-hot: var(--iw-th-rule);

  /* Accents — aliases onto the themable -th- layer above. */
  --iw-gold:     var(--iw-th-accent);
  --iw-gold-dim: var(--iw-th-accent-dim);
  --iw-ember:    var(--iw-th-cta);
  --iw-ember-hi: var(--iw-th-cta-hi);

  /* Text */
  --iw-text:   #DDD6C6;
  --iw-text-hi:#F0E8D6;
  --iw-dim:    #938A79;
  --iw-faint:  #666052;

  /* Semantic */
  --iw-good: #82B88A;
  --iw-bad:  #D27171;
  --iw-info: #75A8C8;

  /* Tier colours */
  --iw-t-common:    #B9B4A8;
  --iw-t-uncommon:  #6FBF73;
  --iw-t-rare:      #5B9BD5;
  --iw-t-epic:      #B98FE0;
  --iw-t-legendary: #D98A3A;
  --iw-t-mythic:    #E06666;

  /* Typography */
  --iw-font-head: 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif;
  --iw-font-ui:   'Barlow', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
  --iw-font-flav: 'Crimson Text', Georgia, serif;

  /* Geometry — intentionally restrained. Round pills are not the house style. */
  --iw-r-panel:   3px;
  --iw-r-control: 2px;
  --iw-r-slot:    2px;
  --iw-r:         var(--iw-r-control);
  --iw-r-sm:      var(--iw-r-slot);

  /* Assumed interval between the game's Current Action progress writes. It is
     the transition duration that turns that staircase into a true 0->100%
     linear ramp (see ui-system.css); UIFoundation measures the real interval
     live and overrides it, continuously, via an inline --iw-progress-duration
     once it has enough samples. Only the pre-measurement fallback lives
     here. */
  --iw-action-tick: 1s;

  /* Game theme tokens */
  --background:          var(--iw-ink-900) !important;
  --foreground:          var(--iw-text)    !important;
  --card:                var(--iw-ink-800) !important;
  --card-foreground:     var(--iw-text)    !important;
  --popover:             var(--iw-ink-800) !important;
  --popover-foreground:  var(--iw-text)    !important;
  --panel-bg:            var(--iw-ink-800) !important;
  --panel-border:        var(--iw-line)    !important;
  --surface-bg:          var(--iw-ink-700) !important;
  --surface-border:      var(--iw-line)    !important;
  --primary:             var(--iw-ember)   !important;
  --primary-foreground:  #FFEAD1           !important;
  --accent:              var(--iw-ember)   !important;
  --accent-foreground:   var(--iw-text-hi) !important;
  --ring:                var(--iw-gold-dim)!important;
  --border:              var(--iw-line)    !important;
  --input:               var(--iw-ink-850) !important;
  --muted:               var(--iw-ink-700) !important;
  --muted-foreground:    var(--iw-dim)     !important;
  --sidebar:             var(--iw-ink-800) !important;
  --sidebar-foreground:  var(--iw-text)    !important;
  --sidebar-border:      var(--iw-line)    !important;
  --sidebar-accent:      var(--iw-ink-700) !important;
}
```

### base-L210 — style

[src/styles/base.css:210](../../src/styles/base.css#L210); ends at line 214.

Styles global theme tokens and host theme aliases.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 195) ── Per-zone frame theme ────────────────────────────────────────────────
> The skin ships nine environment recolours of the skills UI atlas and its
> corner filigree and repaired separator flourish (assets/skills-ui/).
> HeaderRenderer.applyZoneTheme() maps the player's current zone to one and overrides these variables INLINE on
> <html>. These declarations are the un-themed fallback: a zone that has not
> classified yet, or one with no theme, resolves here.
> 
> --iw-zone-atlas      the sheet SkillsArtService's --fs-skills-ui-atlas and
> inventory.css read their sprite windows from
> --iw-corner-filigree the border-image source ui-system.css, header.css and
> tooltip-engine.css all draw their four corners from
> --iw-zone-separator  inventory.css's title divider ornament
> 
> Keep every theme atlas at skills_ui_atlas.webp's 860x463 geometry or the
> sprite-window audit and skills_ui_index.json stop describing it.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 3 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
:root {
  --iw-zone-atlas: url('../assets/skills_ui_atlas.webp');
  --iw-corner-filigree: url('../assets/inventory/panel_corners.webp');
  --iw-zone-separator: url('../assets/inventory/separator_flourish.webp');
}
```

### base-L230 — style

[src/styles/base.css:230](../../src/styles/base.css#L230); ends at line 238.

Styles header identity, navigation and zone chrome.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 216) ── Per-zone accent palettes ───────────────────────────────────────────
> Nine hand-tuned recolours of the --iw-th-* accent layer, one per
> environment family (assets/skills-ui/zone-theme-map.json). Keyed on the
> data-iw-zone-theme attribute HeaderRenderer already sets on <html> for the
> atlas/filigree/separator swap — no JS involved here, pure cascade. `:root[data-…]` is
> (0,1,1), so these beat the (0,0,1) defaults; HeaderRenderer's inline vars on
> <html> only touch the three artwork variables and never collide.
> 
> Rule of thumb per palette: -accent must clear ~4.5:1 on --iw-ink-900, -cta
> must stay in the stock ember's lightness band so --primary-foreground still
> reads on it, and -edge / -rule stay dark enough to be a frame, not a glow.
> State colours (requirement red, quest/skill accents, tier, good/bad/info,
> inventory categories, team colours) are deliberately NOT part of this layer.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,2,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 17 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
:root[data-iw-zone-theme="glacial"] {
  --iw-th-accent: #9FCBE6;  --iw-th-accent-dim: #7C9DB4;
  --iw-th-edge: #45657D;    --iw-th-hairline: #6E96B4;  --iw-th-hairline-hi: #A7CFE6;
  --iw-th-bracket: #A9CADE; --iw-th-bracket-dim: #6E8CA0;  --iw-th-brass: #5C7E96;
  --iw-th-rule: #5E86A0;    --iw-th-rule-soft: #223540;
  --iw-th-plate: #0A0E12;   --iw-th-cta: #356E9A;  --iw-th-cta-hi: #4E90BE;
  --iw-th-ground-a: #14171A;  --iw-th-ground-b: #0B0D10;
  --iw-th-ground-wash: rgba(126,164,192,.055);  --iw-th-glow: rgba(150,200,230,.10);
}
```

<a id="base-L336"></a>

### base-L336 — style

[src/styles/base.css:336](../../src/styles/base.css#L336); ends at line 342.

Styles header identity, navigation and zone chrome.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 320) ── Derived inner frames ───────────────────────────────────────────────
> The nine palettes above set --iw-th-edge and nothing else about frames.
> Everything the skin draws INSIDE a panel steps down from that one value
> here, so a palette added later inherits the whole scale for free and the
> page never mixes a themed outer frame with brass-brown inner boxes.
> 
> Keyed on the bare attribute, not the nine names: (0,1,1) beats the (0,0,1)
> stock defaults, and it cannot collide with the palette blocks (also (0,1,1))
> because those never declare these tokens. Custom properties resolve lazily,
> so `var(--iw-th-edge)` here reads whatever the palette won with regardless of
> source order.
> 
> --iw-line / --iw-line-hi come along because base.css feeds them to the
> game's OWN Tailwind border tokens (--border, --panel-border, --surface-bg's
> partner --surface-border): re-pointing them is what carries the zone colour
> into every game-drawn edge the skin never classified.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,2,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 5 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
:root[data-iw-zone-theme] {
  --iw-th-edge-mid:   color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 66%, var(--iw-ink-850));
  --iw-th-edge-soft:  color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 42%, var(--iw-ink-850));
  --iw-th-edge-faint: color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 26%, var(--iw-ink-850));
  --iw-line:          var(--iw-th-edge-soft);
  --iw-line-hi:       color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 84%, var(--iw-ink-850));
}
```

> all use it. Give every one of them the same textured ground as the

> its own hunt-and-reskin round trip. A surface that wants MORE than the

### base-L452 — style

[src/styles/base.css:452](../../src/styles/base.css#L452); ends at line 456.

Styles header identity, navigation and zone chrome. :is()/:not() contribute their most specific argument; exclusions are also part of the specificity contract.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 433) ── Controls ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

> (line 435) Forged base colour for controls.
> Deliberately ONE element-selector of specificity (0,0,1) and NOT !important:
> any colour the game sets itself — a Tailwind bg-* utility, an inline style,
> a cosmetic chat-name gradient — outranks this and still wins. It exists only
> to catch buttons the game leaves unpainted, which previously fell through to
> the user agent's light `buttonface` and rendered as a pale box with our dark
> gradient laid over it. Found by build-tools/render-fixtures.mjs.
> 
> That "the game still wins" reasoning holds only for a colour the game sets
> ON THE BUTTON. It is FALSE for one the game sets on an ANCESTOR and expects
> to inherit, because a declaration targeting the element itself beats an
> inherited value outright — specificity and importance never enter into it.
> The player name is exactly that shape: the game colours the <h1> and the
> text lives in a nested <button>, so this rule (not any header.css rule) was
> what repainted it. The exclusion is wrapped in `:where()` so the selector
> stays at its deliberate (0,0,1); a bare `:not()` would lift it to (0,1,1)
> and start outranking the game's own `text-*` utilities on every button.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,0,1)`, `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`color`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`background-color`).

```css
button:not(:where([data-iw-header="profile-name"] button)),
[role="button"]:not(:where([data-iw-header="profile-name"] *)) {
  background-color: var(--iw-ink-750);
  color: var(--iw-text);
}
```

<a id="base-L466"></a>

### base-L466 — style

[src/styles/base.css:466](../../src/styles/base.css#L466); ends at line 483.

Styles the exact host/extension elements matched by this selector.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 458) A handful of controls (leaderboard player names so far) are Tailwind
> `hover:underline` text links wearing a <button> tag, not real controls --
> the game gives them no plate of their own, just colour + underline-on-hover.
> Every generic control rule above already opts them out via the
> `hover:underline` clause in its `:not()` chain; this closes the one
> remaining gap, the unguarded base `button` rule two lines up, so they read
> as plain text rather than "a button minus its gradient". Colour is left
> alone -- it is the game's own per-player identity (rule 5).


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`background-color`, `border`, `box-shadow`, `border-radius`).

```css
[class*="hover:underline"] {
  /* `background-color`, NOT the `background` shorthand. The shorthand resets
     EVERY background longhand, including `background-image` and
     `background-clip` — and the game paints the header player name (a
     `hover:underline` button, like these) with a clip-text gradient: a
     `background-image` shown through transparent glyphs. The shorthand wiped
     both and the name rendered BLANK, which reads as "the skin deleted the
     text", not as a background rule overreaching. The plate this rule exists
     to remove is only ever a background-COLOUR here (from the base `button`
     rule above); ui-system.css's gradient plate already opts these out via the
     `hover:underline` clause in its :not() chain. Measured: revert to the
     shorthand and the name goes blank. */
  background-color: transparent !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
}
```

### tooltip-engine-L27 — style

[src/styles/tooltip-engine.css:27](../../src/styles/tooltip-engine.css#L27); ends at line 46.

Styles the exact host/extension elements matched by this selector.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 1) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> Tooltip engine — rich item-card treatment
> 
> The card is a FRAMED SURFACE, and it is framed the way every other framed
> surface in the skin is (see ui-system.css, "Shared forged frame"): the same
> forged ground (texture over the ink gradient, soft-light blended), the same
> gold hairline across its head, the same four mirrored corners from
> assets/inventory/panel_corners.webp, the same Cinzel headings and the same
> 2px control radius. Before this it drew its own flat plate, pill badges and
> a bright white art frame, which is why it read as a different object.
> 
> Two things make the corner filigree work on a card this small:
> 
> 1. It is drawn on the CARD's ground at z-index 0, with the three zones
> (head / body / foot) above it at z-index 1 — the same ordering the
> shared frame uses, where ornament losing to content is the safe
> failure. The head and foot washes are therefore TRANSLUCENT rgba, not
> the opaque plates they used to be: an opaque zone background would bury
> the corners inside it and the card would look unframed again.
> 2. The corner is scaled to the card (--fs-tip-corner-*), not to a panel.
> A card with the panels' 30x28 corners has the ornament eating a third
> of its head; keep the slice at `50%` (it consumes the whole sheet at any
> source density, so only the four corners paint) and bring the
> border-width down with it.
> ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Uses `inline` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`, `margin`). Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`font`, `line-height`, `font-weight`, `letter-spacing`, `text-transform`, `color`, `text-decoration`, `vertical-align`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`background`, `border`, `border-bottom`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow`). Controls motion or geometric transformation (`transition`). Controls hit-testing, interaction affordance or native control appearance (`cursor`).

```css
.iw-item-ref {
  display: inline;
  background: none !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  border-bottom: 1px solid transparent !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  margin: 0 !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  font: inherit !important;
  line-height: inherit !important;
  font-weight: 700 !important;
  letter-spacing: inherit !important;
```

```css
.iw-tip {

}
```

<a id="inventory-L31"></a>

### inventory-L31 — style

[src/styles/inventory.css:31](../../src/styles/inventory.css#L31); ends at line 34.

Styles inventory rows, filters or native action controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 1) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> Inventory / ItemRow — reusable owned-item presentation
> 
> Inventory is the reference implementation for reusable RPG item rows.
> React-owned commands remain live DOM nodes; the Fantasy Skin owns the
> item presentation and semantic action treatment only.
> 
> ── Forged pass, 2026-08-25 ──────────────────────────────────────────
> Ornament is spent where it appears ONCE per panel — the corner filigree,
> the title flourish, the four tool buttons. Everything that repeats per
> row stays plain: a flat socket carrying a rarity edge, and four flat
> action weights. An ornate frame is memorable once and noisy five times.
> 
> Two hard constraints this file works around, both learned from source:
> 
> 1. AtlasService writes background-image / -position / -size INLINE on
> .fs-inv-icon, and appends .iw-icon-badge as a real child. So the
> socket's rarity treatment is border + box-shadow only — never a
> background layer, which inline style would win anyway — and
> overflow stays visible so the enhancement sprite can overhang.
> 
> 2. The action controls are React-owned siblings of the overlay inside
> .compact-row, not children of .fs-inv-row. They are styled in place.
> ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> (line 26) ── Inventory chrome ───────────────────────────────────────────────

> (line 27) The panel ground, the gold hairline, the corner filigree and the padding
> that clears them are NOT here. They live once, in ui-system.css, under the
> shared forged-frame rule that also covers Quests, Market, Skill Actions and
> every other named panel. Inventory only adds what is specific to it.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 1 custom property; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements. Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`overflow`).

```css
[data-iw-inventory-root="1"] {
  --fs-inv-command-w: 54px;
  overflow: hidden !important;
}
```

<a id="inventory-L44"></a>

### inventory-L44 — style

[src/styles/inventory.css:44](../../src/styles/inventory.css#L44); ends at line 60.

Styles inventory rows, filters or native action controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 36) Inner frame around the item list — the same relationship the Quests panel
> has with its quest cards: an ornate outer section frame (corner filigree +
> gold hairline, from ui-system.css) enclosing a recessed inner card that
> carries the skill-card ground. InventoryRenderer tags the game's own row
> wrapper (`div.space-y-1.5`, a sibling of the header / tabs / pagers) with
> data-iw-inventory-list; nothing is reparented. Ground recipe is identical to
> `.fs-quest-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"]` and the shared forged frame:
> texture over the themed --iw-th-ground gradient, soft-light blended.

Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-radius`, `background`, `background-blend-mode`, `box-shadow`). Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`isolation`).

```css
    radial-gradient(circle at 18% 0%, rgba(255,255,255,.03), transparent 34%),
```

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 106) Title flourish — a centred ornament on a full-width hairline, matching the
> concept. It lives on .fs-inv-rule, an element InventoryRenderer appends after
> the header row, because the heading itself sits two flex wrappers deep and a
> pseudo there can never span the panel.
> The ornament is drawn at native proportion; stretching a centre ornament
> smears it, which is what the first attempt did.
> 
> Curtis (2026-09): the flourish's lower point was touching the filter-tab /
> pager row directly beneath it. Both pseudo-elements were centred at
> `top: 50%` of this box (15px), which put the 62px-tall ornament's bottom tip
> 4px past this element's own bottom edge and only 6px shy of the
> `margin-bottom` boundary — the row below sits right at that boundary, so the
> tip's last couple of rows of ink land on it. Fixed with two small,
> independent moves rather than one big one: the shared anchor (`top`, kept in
> px so it doesn't drift if `height` ever changes) moves up 6px, and
> `margin-bottom` grows 6px, splitting the fix between "give the flourish more
> headroom" and "give the row below more clearance" — either alone would work,
> together neither has to do all of it. `top` stays identical on ::before and
> ::after so the line and the ornament riding on it stay concentric.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,1,0)`.

**Effect:** Establishes positioning/containing-box offsets (`position`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`height`, `margin`). Controls hit-testing, interaction affordance or native control appearance (`pointer-events`).

```css

  position: relative;
  height: 30px;
  margin: 2px 0 16px;
  pointer-events: none;
}
```

### inventory-L329 — style

[src/styles/inventory.css:329](../../src/styles/inventory.css#L329); ends at line 353.

Styles inventory rows, filters or native action controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 285) THE ROW HAS THREE CONTROLS AND ONE ORNAMENT, and the game says so itself.
> Live DOM (claude/probe-inventory-toolrow.js):
> 
> <div class="flex items-center gap-2">           <- row, h=37
> <div class="relative"><button …/></div>       <- Filter,    y=222 h=31
> <button aria-label="Search inventory" …/>     <- Search,    y=225 h=31
> <button aria-label="Equipment Window" …/>     <- Equipment, y=225 h=31
> <svg class="lucide lucide-package … text-ember">  <- ornament, 16x16
> </div>
> 
> The three buttons carry `cursor: pointer`, an aria-label and a title. The
> package glyph is a BARE <svg> with `cursor: auto`, no role, no tabindex, no
> aria-label and no title, and the game gives it none of the button chrome it
> gives the other three. That is the game drawing a distinction, and
> CLAUDE.md's rule 5 says the skin must not repaint it away: framing the glyph
> would invent a click affordance the game does not offer. It stays unframed
> and is only harmonised — see the `glyph` rule below.

> (line 303) The three real tool buttons keep the forged frame — they appear once, in the
> corner, which is the one place a framed button still earns its keep.
> `display: grid` + `place-items: center` is load-bearing TWICE; do not drop it
> back to the browser's default button layout.
> 
> 1. THE GLYPH. Tailwind preflight ships `svg { display: block }` on the live
> page, so the icon is a BLOCK child of the button, not inline content — and
> a block box with an explicit width gets no auto-centring, it sits flush
> left. Measured against preflight: every glyph sat at dx = -7.5px, exactly
> half its own 15px width, hard against the left edge of the 30px frame.
> A button does not centre a block child for you; this does.
> 
> 2. THE ROW. Only TWO of the three controls are direct flex children of the
> row — Filter is wrapped in a bare `div.relative` (its dropdown anchor), so
> it is never blockified and lays out in that wrapper's INLINE formatting
> context. Measured live, the wrapper came out 37px around a 31px button
> with the button flush to its top, and the row's `items-center` then
> centred a 37px wrapper against 31px siblings: the 3px the funnel sat high
> (y=222 against 225). Making the button itself block-level leaves the
> wrapper no inline content to build a line box from, so it collapses to the
> control's own height and all three land level.
> 
> This replaced a `:has(> …)` rule on the WRAPPERS that reached the same
> blockification the long way round. Fixing the control itself is tighter (it
> cannot match some other container in another layout) and it is the only one
> of the two that also centres the glyph.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,2,0)`.

**Effect:** Uses `grid !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`place-items`, `flex`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`width`, `height`, `min-width`, `min-height`, `padding`). Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`color`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-radius`, `background-color`, `background`, `background-image`, `background-repeat`, `background-size`, `background-position`, `box-shadow`). Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`overflow`).

**Repeated properties in this block:** `background-repeat`; preserve their order and importance.

```css
[data-iw-inventory-root="1"] [data-iw-inventory-control="icon"] {
  display: grid !important;
  place-items: center !important;
  width: 30px !important;
  height: 31px !important;
  min-width: 30px !important;
  min-height: 31px !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  color: var(--iw-gold-dim) !important;
  background-color: transparent !important;
  /* `background` (shorthand) rather than background-image, so the game's
     bg-white/5 colour and ui-system's gradient are both reset in one go
     instead of layering underneath the atlas. */
  background: var(--iw-zone-atlas) no-repeat !important;
  background-image: var(--iw-zone-atlas) !important;
  background-repeat: no-repeat !important;
  background-size: 322.5px 173.63px !important;
  background-position: -177.38px -2.25px !important;
  background-repeat: no-repeat !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  flex: 0 0 auto !important;
  overflow: visible !important;
}
```

```css
.fs-inv-row {
  /* Identity colour, keyed off the item's SUPER-TYPE (game `category`), not its
     material tier. Set per `.fs-cat-*` below; drives the name text and, through
     --fs-frame, every frame accent. Unresolved items keep this stone default. */
  --fs-tier: #8C8578;
  /* Frame accent (rail, icon border + glow, hover tint). Defaults to the

  min-height: 60px;

  grid-template-areas: "icon body qty";
  align-items: center;
  column-gap: 12px;
  padding: 7px 8px 7px 14px;
  position: relative;
  cursor: default;
```

> (line 723) The row action controls (Equipped / List / Use / Equip / set bonus / lock)
> share ONE plate with the panel's filter tabs and pagers — same border,
> ground, inner shadow, font metrics and uppercase treatment as the
> `[data-iw-inventory-control="filter"]` rule above. Curtis: "they should all
> match and have the same style." Width is content-driven (padding only, no
> fixed `width`) exactly like the filter tabs, so a long label such as
> "✦ set bonus" is never clipped. The per-kind blocks below then layer only a
> state accent on top — the same relationship the active filter tab has with
> its siblings.

```css
}
```

### skillpanel-L42 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:42](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L42); ends at line 79.

Styles skill cards and their native controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 22) ── The forged plate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
> Per Curtis (2026-09) every CONTROL inside a skill card wears the same
> surface as the inventory filter / tool rail: a near-black plate under a
> thin dark-gold rule, with ONE ember plate for the live control — exactly
> the way the active filter tab is the only warm plate in the inventory row.
> The values are lifted verbatim from `[data-iw-inventory-control="filter"]`
> and its `[data-iw-inventory-filter-state="active"]` override in
> `inventory.css`; if that row is ever re-toned, re-tone these with it.
> 
> This supersedes two earlier directions, both of which are now gone from the
> card: the per-skill `--fs-skill-accent` fill on the action button (accent
> still carries discipline identity on the card's left rail, title, medallion
> and level underline, so nothing is lost by taking it off the button), and
> the cool steel plate on the pager arrows.
> 
> `SkillPanelRenderer.styleButton()` writes these same declarations INLINE
> with `!important`, which outranks every rule below — the copies here are the
> pre-render fallback and the two must be kept in step. So must the mirror in
> `build-tools/render-fixtures.mjs`, or the fixture renders a control the game
> never shows.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,2,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 16 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
.compact-panel.fs-skill-panel {
  --fs-forge-bg: linear-gradient(180deg, #100E0A, #0A0907);
  --fs-forge-line: var(--iw-th-edge-faint);
  --fs-forge-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, .035),
    inset 0 -7px 10px -8px rgba(0, 0, 0, .95);
  --fs-forge-ink: var(--iw-text, #DDD6C6);

  --fs-forge-live-bg: linear-gradient(180deg, #1B150B, #120E07);
  --fs-forge-live-line: var(--iw-th-brass);
  /* Per Curtis (2026-09) the live action button's GLOW carries the discipline
     colour, so the bloom, the 1px ring and the label glow are all mixed from
     `--fs-skill-accent` (the ember `#D8791F` is only the pre-classify fallback).
     The plate itself — bg + brass line — stays neutral-warm: one lit plate per
     card, now lit in the skill's own hue. Keep in step with FORGE in
     SkillPanelRenderer.js and render-fixtures.mjs. */
  --fs-forge-live-tint: var(--fs-skill-accent, #D8791F);
  --fs-forge-live-shadow:
    inset 0 0 12px -2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--fs-forge-live-tint) 55%, transparent),
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 216, 150, .18),
    0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--fs-forge-live-tint) 16%, transparent);
  --fs-forge-live-ink: #F3E3C0;
  --fs-forge-live-glow: 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--fs-forge-live-tint) 48%, transparent);

  --fs-forge-hot-line: var(--iw-line-hot, #806337);
  --fs-forge-hot-ink: var(--iw-text, #DDD6C6);

  /* Pager chevron: a `--fs-chev-box` square with `--fs-chev-stroke` borders on
     two adjacent edges, rotated 45deg. `--fs-chev-ink` is the derived shift
     that puts the resulting ink bbox — not the box — on the button centre; see
     the pager block at the end of this sheet for the derivation. */
  --fs-chev-box: 6px;
  --fs-chev-stroke: 2px;
  --fs-chev-ink: calc((var(--fs-chev-box) - var(--fs-chev-stroke)) * 0.3535534);
  --fs-forge-hot-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, .05),
    inset 0 0 10px -3px rgba(216, 121, 31, .35);
}
```

Disabled tests distinguish action availability; a :not() branch excludes rather than selects that state. :is()/:not() contribute their most specific argument; exclusions are also part of the specificity contract.

```css
  color: #FFF6E2 !important;
}
```

```css
  inset: 4px !important;
  z-index: 0 !important;
  pointer-events: none !important;
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 62%, transparent) !important;
  border-radius: 2px !important;
  background: none !important;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 12px rgba(0,0,0,.26) !important;
}
```

### skillpanel-L1164 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:1164](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L1164); ends at line 1183.

Styles skill cards and their native controls. Pseudo-element branches paint generated boxes; their positioning, content and pointer behavior depend on the originating element.

**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,4,1)`.

**Effect:** Uses `none !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Establishes positioning/containing-box offsets (`inset`, `left`, `top`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`width`, `height`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `background-color`, `background-image`, `background-size`, `background-position`, `background-repeat`, `box-shadow`). Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`z-index`). Controls motion or geometric transformation (`transform`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"] .fs-skill-medallion-art::before {
  /* The atlas medallion is quest chrome. Skill identities already own a
     discipline-coloured circular socket; painting the shared quest ring here
     creates a second, floating ring when compact overrides resize the pseudo. */
  display: none !important;
  inset: -11px -8px !important;
  width: auto !important;
  height: auto !important;
  left: -8px !important;
  top: -11px !important;
  transform: none !important;
  z-index: 2 !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  background-color: transparent !important;
  background-image: var(--fs-skills-ui-atlas) !important;
  background-size: var(--fs-ui-medallion-frame-size) !important;
  background-position: var(--fs-ui-medallion-frame-position) !important;
  background-repeat: no-repeat !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
}
```

> inline `!important` outranks every rule in this file. Rather than leave two
> contradicting skins in the sheet, the pager's sprite layer is gone and the
> forged plate is its surface — CLAUDE.md's "a sprite frame on a button means
> the button's own plate must go", run the other way. Any attempt to give the
> pager its sprite back has to drop `background` from the nav-button branch of
> styleButton() at the same time, or it silently does nothing.
> 
> The ACTION button went the other way in 2026-09 — see the sprite section

```css
}
```

### skillpanel-L1935 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:1935](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L1935); ends at line 1942.

Styles skill cards and their native controls. :is()/:not() contribute their most specific argument; exclusions are also part of the specificity contract.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 1911) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> Skills alignment pass — real command stacking + true artwork ratios
> 
> Two defects fixed here, both traceable to the same root cause: the
> fixture used to place `nav-group` inside the CONTENT zone, which no live
> panel does. Live IdleWorlds puts the nav pair and the action control in
> one command cell. The layout above therefore faked the stack with
> `position:absolute` on the nav group and a hard-coded
> `transform: translateY(26px)` on the action button — which skews the real
> DOM (the button is nudged by a fixed 26px unrelated to the nav's height,
> and panels with NO nav are nudged too, so nothing lines up).
> 
> 1. The command cell is now an ordinary centred flex column. Nav sits
> above the action button because it is ordered so, not positioned so.
> 2. Every atlas-backed box is restored to its sprite's real aspect ratio.
> `SkillsArtService` stretches each sprite to exactly fill its element
> (a percentage background-size pair), so a box whose ratio disagrees
> with the art distorts it — the XP plaque was 4.35:1 against 3.00:1
> art, which squeezed the flared ends inward over the text and is why
> "Base: N" read as cramped. Native sizes: xp_plaque 300x100 (3.00),
> action_frame 264x75 (3.52), nav_frame 80x83 (0.96).
> ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> (line 1934) ── Command rail: genuine flow, no absolute nav, no translate ────────


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,4,1)`.

**Effect:** Uses `flex !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`flex-direction`, `align-items`, `justify-content`, `gap`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-layout="three-zone"] [data-iw-skill-zone="commands"]:not(button) {
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column !important;
  align-items: center !important;
  justify-content: center !important;
  gap: 8px !important;
  padding: 8px 14px !important;
}
```

### skillpanel-L2043 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:2043](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L2043); ends at line 2047.

Styles skill cards and their native controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 2022) ══ Command button: the quest rail's artwork ═════════════════════
> Per Curtis (2026-09) the skill command button wears the SAME frame the quest
> rail does — one action-button skin across the site. The sprite itself is
> written INLINE by SkillPanelRenderer's ACTION_ART, because styleButton()'s
> inline `!important` plate outranks every rule in this file and no selector
> here could paint over it; these rules own only what nothing inline contends
> for. Keep the two in step, plus the fixture's copy.
> 
> The studs go with the plate. They are the plate's ornament — the art carries
> its own end flourishes, and a diamond floating 4px off a frame that has
> already tapered to transparent reads as a stray mark. The rules above are
> left in place (this project keeps superseded rules rather than deleting them,
> and `tests/static-invariants.test.mjs` pins their presence); the suppression
> below is gated on the atlas being ready, so a panel that never resolves art
> still gets the studded plate it always had.
> 
> Ratio: action_frame is 264x75 (3.52) and a percentage background-size pair
> stretches the cell to exactly fill its box, so the button's geometry
> ("True artwork ratios" above) is what keeps the frame undistorted — 155x44
> and the 148x44 narrow variant. Do not change either without re-deriving from
> 3.52.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,4,1)`.

**Effect:** Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`filter`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"] button[data-iw-skill-role="action-button"] {
  /* The shadow follows the art's alpha, not the box — the same move the quest
     rail makes once its sprite is on. */
  filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, .45)) !important;
}
```

```css
}
```

### skillpanel-L2525 — style

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 2502) ── The chevron, and why it is positioned ABSOLUTELY ──────────────────
> `place-items: center` on the button does NOT centre this pseudo-element,
> for the reason CLAUDE.md already records for the quest reward plaque: the
> native `‹`/`›` glyph is still in the button (suppressed, not removed), so in
> a GRID it is a second anonymous item on its own row, both auto rows stretch
> to share the 44px, and the chevron ends up centred in the TOP row. Measured
> in the fixture it sat 8.3px above the button's centre — which is exactly the
> "chevron is not centred in the button" report. Taking the pseudo out of flow
> is the fix that cannot be re-broken by whatever the game leaves in the
> button; `place-items` is kept only for the (blockified) glyph child.
> 
> Then the ink. The box is a square with borders on two ADJACENT edges, so
> its ink is an L hugging the far corner, not a centred mark: rotated 45deg
> the ink bounding box is `(box + stroke)/sqrt2` across by `2*box/sqrt2` tall,
> and its centre sits `(box - stroke)/(2*sqrt2)` along the pointing axis from
> the box centre — 1.414px at 6px/2px. Vertically the bbox is symmetric, so
> only the pointing axis needs the shift. `--fs-chev-ink` derives it; do not
> round it to a whole pixel, and do not "tidy" it into the transform, because
> both re-break the moment the box or stroke changes. `box-sizing` is declared
> here rather than inherited: the live page ships Tailwind preflight
> (border-box) and a harness that does not would put the ink 0.7px further
> out, which is exactly the class of fixture lie this file keeps warning
> about. `::after` is left disabled; only `::before` draws.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,6,3)`, `(0,5,2)`.

**Effect:** Uses `block !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-right-width`, `border-bottom-width`, `background`, `box-shadow`). Controls motion or geometric transformation (`transition`). Controls hit-testing, interaction affordance or native control appearance (`pointer-events`). Generates pseudo-element text/artwork content (`content`).

### skillpanel-L2902 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:2902](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L2902); ends at line 2931.

Styles quest cards and their native commands.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 2879) ── Reward chip: a plain plate, not the ornate horned plaque ──────────
> Curtis (2026-09): the 3-slice `skills_xp_plaque_wide.webp` frame (horns +
> flared studs) read as gaudy against the rest of the quest card and was
> dropped for a flat bordered chip — the same "carved slate" language the
> sigil's percentage badge and the skill base-EXP readout already use
> elsewhere on this page, just sized for this label. Still FLEX (not grid):
> the native "Reward: ..." text stays in the node as the accessible copy at
> font-size: 0, and a GRID gives that leftover text node its own row (see the
> CLAUDE.md note on `place-items: center` + a text-node sibling); row-flex
> keeps it a zero-width sibling instead. `--fs-plaque-h` stays the sizing
> knob so the two responsive breakpoints below don't need to change.
> The label length problem the old comment described is still real —
> "+1,875g • +810 combat XP" vs "+2,250g • +1944 tailoring XP" differ by
> ~30px — but a flat chip just stretches with `width: auto` + padding;
> nothing here is sliced from a fixed-ratio sprite any more so there is no
> distortion to guard against.
> 
> A flat chip sidesteps the whole distortion problem the old plaque had:
> `SkillsArtService` sizes atlas sprites with a PERCENTAGE background-size
> pair that stretches a cell to exactly fill its box, and `border-image`
> stretches a fixed-ratio sheet's slices the same way — both need the box's
> aspect ratio to match the art or it distorts. A plain border + gradient has
> no aspect ratio to protect, so it can just grow with the label.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,3,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 1 custom property; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements. Uses `flex !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`align-self`, `align-items`, `justify-content`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`box-sizing`, `min-width`, `height`, `min-height`, `margin-top`, `padding`). Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`color`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `text-shadow`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-radius`, `background`, `box-shadow`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-quest-panel [data-iw-quest-role="reward"] {
  --fs-plaque-h: 42px;
  align-self: flex-start !important;
  /* FLEX, not grid. The native "Reward: ..." text stays in the node as the
     accessible copy at font-size: 0 -- and in a GRID that leftover text node
     becomes a second, anonymous grid item on its own row. Both rows then
     stretch to share the chip's height, so the label was pushed into the
     top half: measured with a debug tint, its line box sat at 7.0..20.8 in a
     42px-tall box instead of centred. In a row-flex the same text node is a
     zero-width sibling and centring works. */
  display: flex !important;
  align-items: center !important;
  justify-content: center !important;
  box-sizing: border-box !important;
  min-width: 0 !important;
  height: var(--fs-plaque-h) !important;
  min-height: var(--fs-plaque-h) !important;
  margin-top: 4px !important;
  padding: 0 14px !important;
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--fs-quest-accent) 42%, var(--iw-th-edge-soft)) !important;
  border-radius: 3px !important;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.035), rgba(0,0,0,.34)) !important;
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.05),
    inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.5) !important;
  color: #F0D8A6 !important;
  font-family: var(--iw-font-head) !important;
  font-size: 0 !important;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 1px #000 !important;
}
```

<a id="skillpanel-L2997"></a>

### skillpanel-L2997 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:2997](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L2997); ends at line 3036.

Styles quest cards and their native commands.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 2974) == Command rail: the artwork IS the control ==========================
> Both controls carry an action_frame sprite, and once it is painted the
> button's OWN plate has to go. The frame art tapers to transparent over the
> outer ~28px of its 264px cell (measured column alpha: 1% at x=0, 94% by
> x=28), so any border / gradient / box-shadow left underneath shows through
> as a second, squarer rectangle around the art -- which is exactly the
> "old button under the graphic" this rail used to draw. The base rules below
> therefore keep that plate ONLY as the no-art fallback; every
> [data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"] rule strips it back to the sprite alone and
> moves the drop shadow into `filter`, so the shadow follows the art's alpha
> instead of the box.
> 
> Geometry: action_frame is 264x75 (3.52). A percentage background-size pair
> stretches the cell to exactly fill the box, so the box has to hold that
> ratio or the frame distorts. `aspect-ratio` keeps it at every rail width;
> min-width 176 puts the resting size at 176x50, comfortably over the 44px
> touch target.
> 
> Skip is the secondary action and takes the DESATURATED frame
> (action_frame_disabled -- grey metal, no gold), which is a hierarchy cue,
> not a state cue. Its real :disabled state stays distinct: rule 5 says the
> skin may not repaint state away, so a disabled Skip additionally loses
> saturation and opacity and takes not-allowed.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,3,0)`, `(0,3,0)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 2 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`align-self`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`box-sizing`, `width`, `max-width`, `min-width`, `height`, `min-height`, `padding`). Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`white-space`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `letter-spacing`, `text-transform`, `text-shadow`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border-radius`). Controls motion or geometric transformation (`transition`). Controls hit-testing, interaction affordance or native control appearance (`cursor`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-quest-panel [data-iw-quest-role="turn-in"],
.compact-panel.fs-quest-panel [data-iw-quest-role="skip"] {
  /* THE HEIGHT IS THE FIXED AXIS AND THE WIDTH FOLLOWS THE LABEL. This is the
     one control on the page whose label length is the GAME's to choose: a work
     order's turn-in reads "Turn In All (38)" and the count is live. The box
     used to be `aspect-ratio: 264/75` over `min-width: 148px`, which grows in
     BOTH axes -- so two cards side by side got different button heights -- and,
     worse, it kept `padding: 0 20px` while the frame's end flourishes are a
     FRACTION of the box (12.9% each side), so past ~155px the horns walked
     inward over the label. That is the reported "TURN IN ALL (38) doesn't fit".
     Now: height fixed, width auto over a 148px floor, and the art is sliced
     (below) so only its flat middle stretches. 148 x 42 is still the resting
     size and still the art's undistorted 3.52.

     One knob per breakpoint. The cap is the width of the sprite's end band,
     derived from the height by the SAME ratio the band's own window uses
     (SkillsArtService, --fs-ui-action-cap-ratio), so the ends never distort.
     The .8 fallback is 60/75 -- the pre-atlas value, so a panel whose art has
     not resolved yet still reserves the right padding. */
  --fs-action-h: 42px;
  --fs-action-cap: calc(var(--fs-action-h) * var(--fs-ui-action-cap-ratio, .8));
  align-self: center !important;
  box-sizing: border-box !important;
  width: auto !important;
  max-width: 100% !important;
  min-width: 148px !important;
  height: var(--fs-action-h) !important;
  min-height: var(--fs-action-h) !important;
  padding: 0 20px !important;
  white-space: nowrap !important;
  border-radius: 3px !important;
  font-family: var(--iw-font-head) !important;
  font-size: 12px !important;
  font-weight: 700 !important;
  letter-spacing: .07em !important;
  text-transform: uppercase !important;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.8) !important;
  cursor: pointer !important;
  transition: filter .12s, border-color .12s, color .12s !important;
}
```

> so a button that grows with its label drags the end flourishes inward over
> the text. This is `border-image`'s three-slice trick done with an ATLAS,
> which border-image itself cannot address (its slices are measured from a
> standalone image's own four edges):
> 
> ::before   the left end band, `--fs-action-cap` wide, at native scale
> element    the flat middle band, stretched across the CONTENT box
> ::after    the right end band, same width, same scale
> 
> Three things are load-bearing here and each is invisible when wrong:`background-origin/clip: content-box` PLUS `padding: 0 var(--fs-action-cap)`.
> The padding IS the cap width, so the middle band paints exactly between
> the two end boxes. Draw it across the whole border box instead and it
> shows THROUGH the horns' transparent taper as a dark rectangle sticking
> out past the frame -- which reads as a stray box, not as a clipping bug.
> The same padding is what keeps the label off the flourishes.`z-index: -1` on the caps, with the button made a stacking context. A
> positioned pseudo-element paints ABOVE its host's inline content, so
> without this the two end bands cover the ends of the label. At negative z
> they paint above the host's own background and below its text, which is
> the order wanted -- the mirror image of the Village medallion trap in
> CLAUDE.md, where that same paint order is what breaks it.The cap BOX is `var(--fs-action-cap)` = height x the band's own source
> ratio, so cap scale == middle scale == vertical scale. Give the caps a
> fixed px width and they distort at every other breakpoint.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,4,0)`, `(0,4,0)`.

**Effect:** Establishes positioning/containing-box offsets (`position`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-radius`, `background-color`, `background-image`, `background-repeat`, `background-origin`, `background-clip`, `box-shadow`, `filter`). Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`isolation`).

```css
.compact-panel.fs-quest-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"] [data-iw-quest-role="turn-in"],
.compact-panel.fs-quest-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"] [data-iw-quest-role="skip"] {
  position: relative !important;
  isolation: isolate !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  padding: 0 var(--fs-action-cap) !important;
  background-color: transparent !important;
  background-image: var(--fs-skills-ui-atlas) !important;
  background-repeat: no-repeat !important;
  background-origin: content-box !important;
  background-clip: content-box !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.45)) !important;
}
```

### skillpanel-L3236 — media

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:3236](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L3236); ends at line 3340.

Conditionally applies its child rules when the viewport, input capability or user preference matches the media query. It does not add selector specificity.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 3216) ── Narrow layout: the LIVE card's format, wearing the skin's art ────────
> Curtis (2026-09): match the vanilla Quests panel's layout on phones, not a
> bespoke stack. The live card reads:
> 
> Title .....................................  [ Turn In ]
> Brief ........................................ [ Skip ]
> ◆ Objective  N/M
> Reward: +g • +XP                    (full width)
> ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    (full-width rail)
> N% complete
> 
> So: the command buttons pin to the TOP-RIGHT of the content row, the text
> lines that sit level with them clear them with padding, and the reward
> plaque + progress rail run the full column width underneath. The forged
> frame, the sigil medallion (slim left rail), the 3-slice reward plaque and
> the action-frame button sprites all stay — just scaled to this rhythm.
> 
> `commands` is the LAST child of `row` in the DOM (no reparenting), so a
> float can't rise beside the earlier text; absolute placement plus targeted
> `padding-right` is what reproduces the wrap.


```css
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  /* Child blocks are fully enumerated in the following entries. */
}
```

**Child blocks:** [skillpanel-L3237](#skillpanel-L3237), [skillpanel-L3248](#skillpanel-L3248), [skillpanel-L3253](#skillpanel-L3253), [skillpanel-L3254](#skillpanel-L3254), [skillpanel-L3261](#skillpanel-L3261), [skillpanel-L3265](#skillpanel-L3265), [skillpanel-L3269](#skillpanel-L3269), [skillpanel-L3287](#skillpanel-L3287), [skillpanel-L3304](#skillpanel-L3304), [skillpanel-L3310](#skillpanel-L3310), [skillpanel-L3311](#skillpanel-L3311), [skillpanel-L3315](#skillpanel-L3315), [skillpanel-L3316](#skillpanel-L3316), [skillpanel-L3322](#skillpanel-L3322), [skillpanel-L3328](#skillpanel-L3328), [skillpanel-L3331](#skillpanel-L3331), [skillpanel-L3335](#skillpanel-L3335), [skillpanel-L3336](#skillpanel-L3336).

<a id="skillpanel-L3411"></a>

### skillpanel-L3411 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:3411](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L3411); ends at line 3418.

Styles skill cards and their native controls.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 3369) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> Skill card composition — full-height identity, right-hand command band
> (Curtis, 2026-09)
> 
> Supersedes every earlier layout pass for the skill card's grid. The card
> had grown ~15 override passes and eight contradicting
> `@media (max-width: 640px)` blocks (lines 811, 1107, 1234, 1304, 1466,
> 1796, 2204, 2516) that disagreed on the grid areas, the command-row height
> and the command flex direction. Below 640px that left the pager + action
> button computing ~131px tall inside a fixed 51px grid track, sheared off by
> the panel's `overflow: hidden`, while the bare-button variant was pinned
> against the left edge of a full-width card. This block is last in the file
> and matches those rules' specificity, so source order carries it.
> 
> Shape, at ALL widths:
> 
> ┌──────────┬──────────────────────┐
> │ medallion│    action title      │   identity spans BOTH rows, so the
> │  SKILL   │    Base: N  reqs     │   icon + level info reach the base
> │  LV n    ├──────────────────────┤   of the card; the content block is
> │  n%  ▓▓▁ │   ‹   ACTION   ›     │   centred in the flexible row above
> └──────────┴──────────────────────┘   the fixed command band.
> 
> THE LOAD-BEARING PART is `--fs-skill-command-h`: the command row is a
> FIXED track pinned to the card's bottom edge, and all three things that
> must line up vertically — the flex command cell, the bare action button,
> and the shape-B pager overlay — are centred on that one band. Make the row
> `auto` again and the two pager shapes drift apart by however much the
> button's own margin differs from the overlay's height, which is exactly
> the ±3px `navFlanksAction` tolerance in render-fixtures.mjs.
> 
> Two React command shapes, presented identically:
> A) pager pair inside the command cell — `nav-group` dissolves to
> `display: contents` and its two arrows become flex siblings of the
> row, ordered prev / action / next.
> B) pager pair left in the CONTENT branch beside the recipe title (it may
> not be reparented) — laid over the command band instead. Both of its
> insets are DERIVED, never guessed: the span is `--fs-skill-command-w`
> (arrow + gap + action + gap + arrow) and the horizontal centre is
> `50% + identity-w/2`, i.e. the centre of the right-hand column, which
> is where the action button itself centres.
> ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,3,1)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 3 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
html .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-layout="three-zone"] {
  /* Not a grid column any more — the width of the centred command CLUSTER
     (arrow + gap + action + gap + arrow), which the shape-B pager spans. */
  --fs-skill-command-w: 240px;
  /* The fixed command band. See the note above before changing it. */
  --fs-skill-command-h: 64px;
  --fs-skill-identity-w: 150px;
}
```

<a id="skillpanel-L3419"></a>

### skillpanel-L3419 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:3419](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L3419); ends at line 3430.

Styles skill cards and their native controls. Direct-child combinators are structure-sensitive: an extra wrapper changes matching.

**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,4,1)`.

**Effect:** Uses `grid !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-template-areas`, `align-items`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`min-height`).

```css
html .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-layout="three-zone"] > [data-iw-skill-layout-shell="1"] {
  display: grid !important;
  grid-template-columns: var(--fs-skill-identity-w, 150px) minmax(0, 1fr) !important;
  grid-template-rows: 1fr var(--fs-skill-command-h, 64px) !important;
  grid-template-areas:
    "identity content"
    "identity commands" !important;
  align-items: stretch !important;
  /* Gives the identity column room to breathe when the content is short;
     a taller card is driven by the content row, which is `1fr`. */
  min-height: 156px !important;
}
```

### skillpanel-L3606 — media

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:3606](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L3606); ends at line 3640.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 3594) ── Phone: the rail narrows so the band still clears the button ────────
> THE CONSTRAINT, because it decides both breakpoints below. The action
> button is 155px WIDE AND `min-width: 155px`, and both are written INLINE
> with `!important` by `SkillPanelRenderer.styleButton()` — no rule in this
> file can shrink it (CLAUDE.md, "Inline `!important` from a renderer
> outranks every stylesheet rule"). So the flanked cluster is a hard
> 26 + gap + 155 + gap + 26 = 215px, and the right-hand column must clear
> that plus its padding: ~223px. Measured in the fixture the card is about
> (viewport − 81)px, so beside-the-rail needs `viewport ≥ 223 + rail + 81`.
> A 78px rail therefore holds from ~382px up — which covers the 390px
> phone — and a 116px rail from ~420px. Widen either rail and
> `skillOverflow` fails at the next width down.


```css
@media (max-width: 430px) {
  /* Child blocks are fully enumerated in the following entries. */
}
```

<a id="skillpanel-L3647"></a>

### skillpanel-L3647 — style

[src/styles/skillpanel.css:3647](../../src/styles/skillpanel.css#L3647); ends at line 3655.

Styles skill cards and their native controls. :is()/:not() contribute their most specific argument; exclusions are also part of the specificity contract.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 3642) ══ Exact themed button states ═══════════════════════════════════════
> The state images in exact-v3 share one alpha mask and canvas per control,
> so interaction changes only lighting. The renderer's inline background
> reads --fs-button-background; changing this inherited custom property does
> not touch layout or React's event ownership.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,6,2)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 3 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements. Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`background`, `filter`).

```css
html[data-iw-zone-theme]:not([data-iw-zone-theme="default"])
  .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skills-ui-ready="1"]
  button[data-iw-skill-role="action-button"] {
  --fs-button-art: var(--iw-action-idle);
  --fs-button-paint: var(--iw-action-idle-paint);
  --fs-button-background: var(--fs-button-paint, transparent var(--fs-button-art) center / 100% 100% no-repeat);
  background: var(--fs-button-background) !important;
  filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, .45)) !important;
}
```

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 3887) ── Below ~382px the cluster cannot sit beside ANY usable rail ─────────
> From the arithmetic above, a card narrower than ~295px leaves the
> right-hand column under 223px however thin the rail gets. There the
> command band spans BOTH columns again (the layout that shipped before
> this pass) and identity keeps a row-1 cell instead of running to the
> card's base. This block must stay AFTER the 430px one to win.
> 
> Do NOT "fix" this by loosening `actionButtonsSized` /
> `navButtonsAccessible` in render-fixtures.mjs — the 44px height and the
> 155px frame are the touch target and the action_frame artwork ratio, not
> slack. The real fix, if the fallback ever needs to go, is de-inlining the
> button geometry in styleButton() so CSS can make it elastic; see
> V1.6.0_MOBILE_LAYOUT_AUDIT.md §8.


```css
@media (max-width: 384px) {
  /* Child blocks are fully enumerated in the following entries. */
}
```

### skillcard-v2-L17 — style

[src/styles/skillcard-v2.css:17](../../src/styles/skillcard-v2.css#L17); ends at line 72.

Styles the V2 skill-card composition.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 1) ============================================================================
> Skill Card V2 — functional concept
> 
> This sheet is intentionally presentation-only. SkillPanelRenderer continues
> to identify and own the native gameplay nodes. V2 only consumes its semantic
> role attributes and skin-owned helper nodes from SkillCardDesignController.
> No new artwork is introduced here.
> ==========================================================================

> (line 10) The V2 card is the only design (Curtis, 2026-09): the old/new switch and
> the "current" mode it selected are gone.

> (line 14) Shared composition. Native game branches remain in place. The additional
> selector is intentional: this design must outrank the later ui-system sheet.
> Keep geometry here; the renderer's inline dimensions resolve these tokens.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,5,1)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 28 custom properties; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements. Establishes positioning/containing-box offsets (`position`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`, `margin-bottom`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`border`, `border-radius`, `background`, `box-shadow`). Controls clipping, stacking or container-query scope (`container`, `overflow`).

```css
html[data-iw-skill-card-design="new"] .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-v2="1"][data-iw-skill-layout] {
  /* The hero group is compact enough to breathe inside its ornamental frame
     (Curtis, 2026-09); the discipline name under it keeps its size. */
  --iw-skill-v2-icon: 43px;
  --iw-skill-v2-ring-gap: 7px;
  --iw-skill-v2-ring-weight: 4px;
  --iw-skill-v2-identity-w: 144px;
  --iw-skill-v2-command-w: 96px;
  --iw-skill-v2-gutter: 20px;
  --iw-skill-v2-rail-bottom: 6px;
  --iw-skill-v2-cmd-buffer: 8px;
  /* The action label, framed button and pager are one centred command stack.
     The icon scales from the button's current dimensions and always preserves
     a safe inset outside its box; the SVGs add their own 4% ink padding. */
  --iw-skill-v2-label-h: 12px;
  --iw-skill-v2-action-label-gap: 4px;
  --iw-skill-v2-glyph-safe-inset: 14px;
  /* The label's CEILING. SkillCardDesignController.fitActionLabel measures
     each label once and writes a smaller size inline on the card whenever the
     text would not fit on one line inside the buffer. */
  --iw-skill-v2-action-label-font: 9.5px;
  /* The game-owned label remains in the real button for its accessible name,
     but occupies no visual layout; the aria-hidden mirror above is painted. */
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-font: 0px;
  --iw-skill-v2-label-buffer: 4px;
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-tracking: .02em;
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-border: 3px;
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-offset: calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-label-h) + var(--iw-skill-v2-action-label-gap));
  --iw-skill-v2-glyph: max(16px, min(calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-w) - var(--iw-skill-v2-glyph-safe-inset) - var(--iw-skill-v2-glyph-safe-inset)), calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-h) - var(--iw-skill-v2-glyph-safe-inset) - var(--iw-skill-v2-glyph-safe-inset))));
  --iw-skill-v2-glyph-inset: calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-offset) + (var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-h) - var(--iw-skill-v2-glyph)) / 2);
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-pad: 0;
  --iw-skill-v2-cmd-stack: calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-offset) + var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-h));
  /* 30% smaller in BOTH axes. Width alone would leave the command column
     needing btn-h + buffer + nav-h + 24px = 148px, which is exactly what held
     every card at 148-152px however small the hero became. */
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-w: 64px;
  --iw-skill-v2-nav-w: 30px;
  --iw-skill-v2-nav-h: 22px;
  --iw-skill-v2-nav-radius: 4px;
  --iw-skill-v2-btn-h: 66px;
  /* The card's frame, dividers and panels follow the CURRENT ZONE (Curtis,
     2026-09) from the shared --iw-th-* layer. Left literal on purpose: the
     met/unmet greens and oranges (rule 5), the skill-accent ring and hero
     wash (identity) and the text colours. */
  --iw-skill-v2-edge: var(--iw-th-edge-mid);
  --iw-skill-v2-edge-soft: var(--iw-th-edge-soft);
  container: iw-skill-card / inline-size !important;
  position: relative !important;
  overflow: visible !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  margin-bottom: 10px !important;
  border: 1px solid var(--iw-skill-v2-edge) !important;
  border-radius: 7px !important;
  background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 0 0, color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-edge) 50%, transparent), transparent 60%), linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-ground-a) 93%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, var(--iw-th-ground-b) 96%, transparent)), url('../assets/skills_panel_texture.webp') center / cover !important;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--iw-th-plate), inset 0 0 0 4px var(--iw-th-edge-soft), 0 4px 12px #0006 !important;
}
```

### skillcard-v2-L86 — style

[src/styles/skillcard-v2.css:86](../../src/styles/skillcard-v2.css#L86); ends at line 108.

Styles the V2 skill-card composition. Relational :has() depends on the specified descendants/siblings still being present. Direct-child combinators are structure-sensitive: an extra wrapper changes matching. :is()/:not() contribute their most specific argument; exclusions are also part of the specificity contract.

**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,6,1)`, `(0,6,1)`.

**Effect:** Uses `grid !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-template-areas`, `gap`, `align-items`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`min-height`).

```css
html[data-iw-skill-card-design="new"] .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-v2="1"][data-iw-skill-layout] > [data-iw-skill-layout-shell="1"],
html[data-iw-skill-card-design="new"] .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-v2="1"][data-iw-skill-layout]:not(:has(> [data-iw-skill-layout-shell="1"])) {
  display: grid !important;
  grid-template-columns: var(--iw-skill-v2-identity-w) minmax(0, 1fr) var(--iw-skill-v2-command-w) !important;
  /* The hero and action columns span every row, so the centre column owns
     three bands - the title row, the info frame and the foot row - between two
     flexible SPACER rows. The spacers take whatever height the hero column or
     the command group adds beyond the centre stack, so the stack sits on the
     card's middle line as one group and the frame hugs its own content. With
     the spare height in the frame's row instead, a card at its floor drew a
     frame nearly twice as tall as its one material. A title-only card is the
     same stack with two empty bands, so it centres by the same rule. */
  grid-template-rows: 1fr auto auto auto 1fr !important;
  grid-template-areas:
    "identity .        commands"
    "identity content  commands"
    "identity body     commands"
    "identity tabs     commands"
    "identity .        commands" !important;
  gap: 0 !important; align-items: stretch !important;
  /* Tall enough for the command group plus a margin, whatever the content. */
  min-height: calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-cmd-stack) + 24px) !important;
}
```

<a id="skillcard-v2-L178"></a>

### skillcard-v2-L178 — style

[src/styles/skillcard-v2.css:178](../../src/styles/skillcard-v2.css#L178); ends at line 188.

Styles the V2 skill-card composition.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 166) The title row: the action name with its BASE chip beside it, centred on the
> text. It is a GRID, not a flex column ordered with `order`, because the two
> are not always siblings: the chip is appended straight into the content zone,
> but live the game wraps the title in a branch of its own, so a rule keyed on
> `> [action-title]` never matched, the wrapper kept the default order, and the
> chip painted ABOVE a centred title. Placing "the branch that holds the title"
> and "the chip" into named cells works for both shapes without moving a node.
> The title track is `minmax(0, max-content)`, so a long name wraps and the chip
> stays beside it rather than being pushed onto a line of its own. The ROW gap
> is 0 on purpose: the zone also holds the game's own zero-height and clipped
> nodes, and each one that lays out as a grid item costs a row, so a 6px row
> gap measured 30px of empty space between the title and the frame.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,6,1)`.

**Effect:** Uses `grid !important` display, determining whether this box lays out as a grid/flex/block, disappears, or passes layout through with contents. Assigns grid/flex tracks, placement or spacing (`grid-area`, `grid-template-columns`, `justify-content`, `align-content`, `align-items`, `gap`). Establishes positioning/containing-box offsets (`position`). Sets sizing and box-model geometry (`padding`). Sets text hierarchy, wrapping or foreground treatment (`text-align`). Paints, masks or clips the surface/artwork (`background`, `box-shadow`).

```css
html[data-iw-skill-card-design="new"] .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-v2="1"][data-iw-skill-layout] [data-iw-skill-zone="content"] {
  grid-area: content !important; display: grid !important;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, max-content) auto !important; justify-content: start !important;
  align-content: center !important; align-items: center !important; gap: 0 12px !important;
  position: static !important;
  /* No ground of its own (Curtis, 2026-09). This zone spans only the title
     row, so a wash here drew a lighter box behind the title that stopped
     short of the card's foot and broke the card into two panels. */
  padding: 14px var(--iw-skill-v2-gutter) 10px !important; background: none !important;
  text-align: left !important; box-shadow: none !important;
}
```

### skillcard-v2-L245 — style

Styles the V2 skill-card composition.

**Immediately preceding source intent:**

> (line 231) Portrait action: existing textured artwork, metal bevel and blue inset.

> (line 232) The command GROUP - the action button, its glyph and the recipe arrows - is
> centred vertically in the card, with a fixed buffer between the button and
> the arrows (Curtis, 2026-09: "the arrow buttons are being hidden underneath
> the action button"). Every part is placed from ONE anchor, the column's
> vertical centre, rather than letting the button sit in flex flow and
> measuring the arrows off wherever it ended up. That is deliberate: live, the
> button sat ~14px lower than in any fixture, so some in-flow node the fixture
> does not model sits above it, and an arrow offset measured from a guess about
> the button's position lands on top of it. Out of flow, nothing else in the
> column can move the button. The pager ships in EITHER branch, and both
> resolve 50% against a box with the card's full height: the commands zone
> spans all three shell rows, and the content zone is static, so a pager there
> resolves against the card.


**Selector specificity, in source branch order:** `(0,5,1)`.

**Effect:** Defines or overrides 1 custom property; inherited token consumers resolve these values on their own elements.

```css
html[data-iw-skill-card-design="new"] .compact-panel.fs-skill-panel[data-iw-skill-v2="1"][data-iw-skill-layout] {
  --iw-skill-v2-cmd-stack: calc(var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-offset) + var(--iw-skill-v2-btn-h));
}
```
